source_name: KSH STADAT – Belkereskedelem (retail turnover tables, bel0001–bel0020)
source_subtype: national statistical office statistical table system
why_relevant: Official monthly/annual retail turnover by store type, region and county — the denominator against which card/cash payment shares and POS acceptance penetration are measured. Retail turnover is the base series for any HU cash-vs-card modelling.

source_name: KSH Belkereskedelem topic hub + Kiskereskedelem gyorstájékoztató (flash report)
source_subtype: statistical office topic portal / press release series
why_relevant: Landing hub that points to the monthly retail flash release, methodology notes and the linked STADAT table list (ksh.hu/stadat_kis). Best single entry point for discovering new/renamed retail tables.

source_name: KSH STADAT – Információ, kommunikáció (IKT) tables, incl. online purchasing by population
why_relevant: The household ICT survey series carries e-commerce incidence and (in the survey publications) payment-method breakdowns for online purchases — a rare non-central-bank measure of payment behaviour.

source_name: KSH ICT publications (A vállalkozások és a háztartások IKT-eszközökkel való ellátottsága és használata)
why_relevant: The narrative ICT/e-commerce publications contain the payment-method-of-online-purchase splits (utánvét/cash-on-delivery vs online card vs transfer vs fintech app) that do not appear as standalone STADAT tables.

source_name: KSH – Helyzetkép a kiskereskedelemről (annual retail situation report)
why_relevant: Annual analytical retail report; historically includes store-network, e-commerce and structural detail useful for POS/acceptance-base sizing.

source_name: KSH Tájékoztatási adatbázis / STATINFO (dissemination database)
why_relevant: Multi-dimensional query interface over KSH time series (retail, ICT, consumption) allowing deeper cuts than the flat STADAT tables; the practical route to custom retail/ICT series.

source_name: KSH Kutatószoba (safe centre) – research microdata access
source_subtype: microdata safe centre / research access programme
why_relevant: Route to household budget (HKÉF) and ICT microdata that would allow payment-behaviour cuts by income, region, age — far beyond published aggregates. Access is contractual, not scrapeable.

source_name: KSH Háztartási költségvetési és életkörülmény adatfelvétel (HKÉF) – income & consumption statistics
why_relevant: Household consumption structure by expenditure group and income decile — the basis for estimating which spending categories remain cash-intensive.

source_name: KSH English STADAT / HCSO English site
why_relevant: English mirror of the same tables and press releases (e.g. e-commerce order incidence and average online spend), useful for reporting and for cross-checking Hungarian labels.

source_name: KSH heti monitor – Kereskedelem (weekly/high-frequency monitor)
why_relevant: High-frequency trade indicators; KSH's experimental fast statistics are the layer most likely to eventually surface cash-register-derived turnover proxies.

source_name: NAV – eNyugta / e-pénztárgép information hub
why_relevant: Authoritative rules, deadlines and data-content specification for the e-receipt / e-cash-register regime (e-pénztárgép operable from 1 July 2025; obligation extension for previously exempt sectors from 1 Sept 2026). Defines what payment-mode telemetry the state now captures at practically every HU retail till.

source_name: NAV – online cash register data download service (machine-to-machine OPG log retrieval)
why_relevant: Documents the M2M service (live since Feb 2023) through which a taxpayer can pull their own cash-register log files — receipt-level records that include payment mode. Establishes that transaction-level cash/card data exists and is machine-retrievable, though scoped to the operator's own tills.

source_name: NAV Adatbázisok / Adóstatisztikák (tax statistics & registries)
why_relevant: NAV's published statistics and yearbooks — VAT/turnover aggregates, sectoral tax data and (for reference) excise volume series published monthly. The natural place any published cash-register aggregates would appear.

source_name: NAV public-data disclosure list – registers maintained by NAV (nyilvántartások)
why_relevant: The statutory inventory of every register NAV keeps — the cheapest way to discover which payment/cash-register datasets exist at all, including ones never published, and therefore what can be requested under freedom-of-information rules.

source_name: NAV Online Számla system – interface specification & public GitHub repo
source_subtype: government API documentation + public issue tracker
why_relevant: The invoice-level reporting regime's schema (v3.x) defines the payment-method enumerations reported to the state; the public GitHub issue tracker is an unusually candid window into how the regime and its data model evolve.

source_name: Nemzeti Közadatportál / National Open Data Portal (opendata.gov.hu, kozadatportal.hu)
why_relevant: The statutory national data-asset portal (operated under the 2023 national data-asset act, implementing rules in force from 1 Sept 2024) where KSH/NAV datasets are catalogued and where 'requestable' public datasets can be applied for — a discovery layer plus a formal request channel.

source_name: kormany.hu – government communications on e-pénztárgép / eNyugta rollout
why_relevant: Ministerial/government announcements set the timetable and policy intent for the fiscal-telemetry regime (free NAV ePénztárgép and eNyugta mobile apps), which directly shapes POS/terminal demand and cash-vs-card measurement.

source_name: Állami Számvevőszék (State Audit Office) analyses – financial awareness & digitalisation
why_relevant: ÁSZ publishes analytical studies touching financial awareness, digitalisation and e-commerce (e.g. the 2021 financial-awareness/digitalisation analysis and a techipar/e-kereskedelem analysis) — public-sector analysis outside the central bank.

source_name: Statisztikai Szemle (KSH methodological journal)
why_relevant: KSH's peer-reviewed journal documents methodology behind the retail turnover series (e.g. the monthly retail turnover article) — essential for correctly interpreting any cash-vs-card share derived from these series.

source_name: GIRO BKR forgalmi statisztika PDF-ek („BKR tranzakciók száma”, /storage/ assets)
why_relevant: The most granular publicly surfaced GIRO series: monthly BKR transaction counts (long history, at least 2000–2022 in observed vintages) split by platform (éjszakai / napközbeni / azonnali elszámolás). This is the raw AFR-uptake and batch-clearing time series.

source_name: GIRO BKR Üzletszabályzat (business rules) és mellékletei, incl. HCT Inst üzenetáramlási folyamatleírás
why_relevant: Defines participation rules, cycle structure, cut-offs, message standards (HCT Inst / SEPA-based) and change history of the clearing system — the structural context needed to interpret volume series and to anticipate scheme changes (e.g. AFR 2.0).

source_name: MNB Statisztika – Fizetési és értékpapír-elszámolási rendszerek működése (VIBER, BKR, KELER idősorok)
why_relevant: The single best structured, downloadable time series covering BKR, VIBER and KELER turnover — regulator-published but sourced from the system operators. Fills the gap left by GIRO's irregular PDF releases and provides value as well as volume.

source_name: MNB Fizetési rendszer jelentés (annual Payment Systems Report)
why_relevant: Annual analytical report on the operation of VIBER and the GIRO-operated BKR, including availability, incident, concentration and turnover analysis, plus commentary on AFR uptake. Interprets operator data the operator itself does not narrate publicly.

source_name: MNB qvik hivatalos oldal és GYIK
why_relevant: qvik is the MNB/GIRO-developed AFR-based QR/deep-link payment scheme layered on GIROInstant; the official site carries scheme rules, participant lists and adoption communication — the key competitive-threat signal for card acquiring and POS.

source_name: KELER Zrt. – Dokumentumtár / Statisztikák (napi, heti, havi, éves)
why_relevant: Hungarian CSD publishes settlement/turnover statistics at daily, weekly, monthly and annual frequency, including machine-readable daily CSVs (OTC_NAPI_YYYYMMDD.csv). This is operator-original securities settlement data that regulators only aggregate later.

source_name: KELER KSZF (KELER CCP) – Financial Reports / Key documents
why_relevant: The Hungarian central counterparty publishes annual reports (observed range 2009–2023) in English with cleared-volume, guarantee-fund and market-coverage detail across BÉT, BÉTa, Xtend, XBond, MTS Hungary and the gas platforms.

source_name: ECB Data Portal – Central Counterparty Clearing Statistics (CCP), Hungary series
why_relevant: Harmonised, machine-readable CCP statistics with explicit Hungarian series keys (HU1 / KEL), enabling cross-country benchmarking of the Hungarian CCP without depending on KELER's own PDF cadence. ECB also hosts the PSS payment-statistics dataset covering Hungarian payment system turnover.
